meta.temperature_K_convention: Pair is [min_K, max_K]. Use null for max to mean no upper bound. A number always means that number — there is no magic threshold. (999 is still read as no-bound for older files, but is deprecated: write null.)

general.description: Organic structures resembling sea urchin shells rather than true anemones. They can tolerate a wide range of temperatures and absorb energy from nearby stars.

species.description: Yellow Anemone of rocky bodies in systems lit by a main-sequence or subgiant B star.

matchContextNotes: Measured 2026-10-05 on 204 confirmed bodies (Spansh dump; the only Anemone body in its system, and EDAstro's codex logs exactly this Anemone species there): rocky 97 %, metal-rich 1 %, high metal content 1 %; airless 96.1 %; main star B V 139, B IV 63, A V 2. A B IV-V star is the main star on 202 of 204 and some star in the system on 204 (any-star gate); 202-1225 K, median 369 K.

Thin atmospheres listed since 2026-10-07 (no misses first): 10 of 313 known-spawn Anemone bodies in the precision sample (new Spansh export) had one and were hidden. The genus prior keeps their chance at what the dump shows (0.6 % of Anemone bodies) and still hides Anemone where the dump has none. Before: airless only. A thin atmosphere (sulphur dioxide, carbon dioxide and others) is under 4 % of each colour's bodies; allowing sulphur dioxide cost 17 bodies whose genera the signal count had decided, on the owner's journals (accuracy probe 2026-09-28), for no species found. The single Anemone row before the split was airless in effect too: its 'Thin (rare, Sulfur Dioxide confirmed)' never parsed to a journal atmosphere.

authorNotes.split: 2026-09-28 (owner's yes): one row per colour. The game logs each colour as its own codex entry (codex_ent_sphere, sphereabcd_01-03, sphereefgh, sphereefgh_01-03) and each has its own habitat, so one 'Anemone' row described a habitat none of them has.
authorNotes.rule: Colour = the star lighting the system (the brightest on the body; in practice the main star) and its luminosity class, times the body: O -> Puniceum (icy) / Prasinum Bioluminescent (rocky, metal); B IV-V -> Luteolum (rocky) / Blatteum Bioluminescent (metal); B I-III -> Roseum (rocky) / Roseum Bioluminescent (metal); B VI or A giant -> Croceum (rocky) / Rubeum Bioluminescent (metal). Enforced by src/shared/hostStarGates.ts.
